Formar o Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war + Pa: Form the Plusquamperfekt (hatte/war + Partizip II), use it for a past that came before another past, and combine it with nachdem and bevor.
Você conta o passado em duas camadas. Pr: You can tell the past in two layers. Next lesson: als × wenn and other time conjunctions.
PASSO 1: o PLUSQUAMPERFEKT é o passado d: STEP 1: the PLUSQUAMPERFEKT is the "past of the past": it tells something that happened BEFORE another past event — the English past perfect ("I had eaten"). STEP 2: form: Präteritum of «haben» or «sein» (hatte / war) + Partizip II at the end: «Ich hatte gegessen» (I had eaten), «Er war gegangen» (he had left). STEP 3: the choice of haben/sein is the same as in the Perfekt: «ich hatte gearbeitet», «ich war gefahren». English always uses "had"; German uses «war» with verbs of movement and change: «er war gegangen». STEP 4: conjugate: ich hatte / war, du hattest / warst, er hatte / war, wir hatten / waren, ihr hattet / wart, sie hatten / waren. STEP 5: helpful words: schon, bereits, vorher, davor, zuerst: «Als ich ankam, hatte der Film schon begonnen» (when I arrived, the movie had already started).
o português tem o mais-que-perfeito comp: English has the same tense: "I had eaten" = «Ich hatte gegessen». Two differences: German uses «war» instead of "had" with movement verbs («er war gegangen» = he had gone), and the participle goes to the end.

PASSO 1: «NACHDEM» (depois que) abre uma: STEP 1: «NACHDEM» (after) opens a subordinate clause: the conjugated verb goes to the END. STEP 2: the event in the subordinate clause happened FIRST, so it goes in the PLUSQUAMPERFEKT; the main clause goes in the Präteritum or Perfekt: «Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, bin ich spazieren gegangen» (after I had eaten, I went for a walk). STEP 3: the same idea in the present: «Nachdem ich gegessen habe, gehe ich spazieren» (Perfekt in the subordinate clause, present in the main clause). STEP 4: if the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause starts with the VERB. STEP 5: always pick the tense of «nachdem» by this rule: ONE STEP BACK from the main clause. English is relaxed here ("after I ate, I left"); German is strict. Also: «nachdem» is a conjunction; the preposition "after" is «nach» («nach dem Essen»).
Nachdem ich aß, bin ich gegangen.

Bevor e a sequência dos fatos: Bevor and the order of events
PASSO 1: «BEVOR» (antes que, antes de) a: STEP 1: «BEVOR» (before) opens a subordinate clause: verb at the end. STEP 2: the tense is the SAME as in the main clause: «Bevor ich ging, habe ich das Licht ausgemacht» (before I left, I turned off the light) or, in the present, «Bevor ich gehe, mache ich das Licht aus.» STEP 3: the contrast: «nachdem» needs the earlier tense; «bevor» uses the same tense. STEP 4: sequence adverbs (verb in 2nd position): «zuerst … dann … danach … zuletzt» (first… then… after that… finally): «Zuerst habe ich gegessen, dann habe ich gearbeitet.» STEP 5: «vorher / davor» (before that) and «nachher / danach» (after that) are also adverbs, with the verb in 2nd position — unlike English "then I worked", German says «dann habe ich gearbeitet».
